through the stormy sound of the Shofar. For those who know Him, there is comfort, it is reckoned a good sign for the establishment of peace through the pleasant sound of the Shofar. They who reject Him will be cut down, the faithless will be uprooted, rebels will sink down through the powerful sound of the Shofar. blocks.text: On Sabbath.

As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem’.

Fasten Thy laws to me lest they fly away like the eagle, lest there take flight those who make heard Thy voice. I will learn the pure law with my eyes on my Teacher just as once His messenger (Moses) spoke and God answered him with His voice.
As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘And the sound of the Shofar grew very powerful, Moses was speaking and God was answering him aloud’.

The end has approached, the time of judgment comes, a defender arises to entreat with his voice. The new moon is sanctified and the feast prepared, so let me blow the Shofar that He may answer me with His voice.
As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘Blow the Shofar on the new moon, when the moon is covered on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob’.

blocks.text: 142 Musaph for the New Year 142

The fourth of the wild beasts (that Daniel saw) will fall into the fire, among the sparking flames at the fiery sound of the Shofar. Thou wilt stir up sleep to pay retribution to the oppressor, and shatter his multitudes with the mighty sound of the Shofar. Thou wilt free the Rose (Israel) and let redemption dawn, revive those who slumber with the rousing sound of the Shofar. Thou wilt march from Hermon to destroy Admon, bring cooling to Tsalmon with the massive sound of the Shofar. Thou wilt step in our midst as once in the wilderness when Thou didst give us the Torah and once again wilt Thou allow to be heard in the Sanctuary a voice that sounds like that of the Shofar.

As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘And it happened on the third day during the morning that there was thunder and lightning and a heavy cloud lay over the mountain and there was a very powerful sound of the Shofar and all the people in the camp were afraid’. And it was said: ‘And the sound of the Shofar grew very powerful, Moses was speaking and God was answering him aloud’. And it was said: ‘And all the people were seeing the thunder and the lightning and the sound of the Shofar and the mountain in smoke, the people saw and trembled and stood at a distance’. verdict: Primary Hebrew for s300/s302/s304 had many errors that the image settles. Consonant misreadings: יֵחָשֵׁב, מְחִיפוֹ, בְגַלָּה, הוּחָה, צֹהַר, לוֹמַר, תָּשׁוּר, רַעַשׁ, יִפְנוּ, שָׁג and others. A systematic error added a yod to every Shabbat stanza ending (קוֹלִי); the print has קוֹל throughout. Primary also dropped every ח׳/חזן role label and missed the article in הַתַּפּוּחַ. Blind was much closer on consonants. Its errors: it misread לִהְיוֹת/לֶהֱיוֹת as לְהָוֹת and תְּיַשֵּׁר as תַּשִּׁיר, and kept role labels and citation linkage inside the text. The English pages s301/s303/s305 match primary except one spurious colon on s305. The closing quote missing on s305 exodus_20_15 is a source misprint and is preserved. Citation verses are set in small square type, not Rashi script; no Rashi-script labels appear on these pages. Weekday (essa → essa_tail → weekday_verses) and Shabbat (anusah_tail … tevunah) runs stay continuous across pages. The listed word-level pointing questions need human review before the readings are accepted; the shabbat_rubric reading (אַם vs חַזָּן) needs it most.
